interpretation: The fixed 10-view fine-crop second-look pass was highly conservative but provided no recall benefit.
All five eligible positive clips also remained negative.
The four temporally covered recognition misses produced zero raw findings despite finer visual crops.
Because no second-look candidates were generated, 42B-2 multiscale verification had nothing new to evaluate.
This candidate should not be promoted.
hypotheses_not_yet_proven: Presenting ten overlapping images in one request may dilute attention across views.
The conservative second-look prompt may suppress subtle but valid conditions.
Some relational or geometric defects may require focused comparison rather than generic open-ended defect discovery.
next_direction: Do not repeat the same 10-view open-ended second-look design.
Run a small diagnostic experiment before spending on another full 17-clip evaluation.
Test whether focused regional questioning can recover the four known covered misses when the relevant visual region is isolated.
Keep any diagnostic label-informed tests separate from performance claims.
If focused recognition succeeds, redesign an annotation-blind production trigger that selects regions/questions without using ground truth.
conclusion: 42B-3 preserved clean precision but recovered 0/4 covered recognition misses, so development performance remains 3/9 verified intervals with 0/13 clean false-positive clips.
status_detail: Fine-crop second-look candidate rejected; redesign required.
